title: plan
description: The planning bundle. `summary` is intentionally typed loosely here — it is the summary payload and is validated against schemas/v3/summary.json in the same run; this validator has no $ref, so cross-file composition happens at the call site rather than being faked with a duplicated copy that would drift.

target_known.description: True when this session carries a structured target on any signal (ADR 0014, ADR 0019); target_kind names the signal. Every magnitude is an impossible-zero field behind this flag (ADR 0009), and a magnitude another kind carries stays 0 or the empty string.

target_kind.description: The signal the target is written on: power watts, a heart-rate band, an HR zone, or a pace. Empty when target_known is false.

target_literal.description: The target in its canonical spelling, e.g. 3x12:00@230W, 1x1:00:00@HR125-147, 1x1:30:00@Z2, 5x4:00@4:10/km, 10x100m@1:40/100m. Empty when target_known is false.

target_dur_s.description: A timed rep's length in seconds; 0 for a distance rep.

target_dist_m.description: A distance rep's length in metres; 0 for a timed rep. Only a pace target carries one.

target_hr_lo.description: The heart-rate band's floor in bpm; hr targets only.

target_hr_hi.description: The heart-rate band's cap in bpm; hr targets only.

target_zone.description: The HR zone, 1-5, under the athlete's configured zones; zone targets only.

target_pace_s.description: Seconds per target_pace_unit; pace targets only.

target_pace_unit.description: The distance a pace reads over; pace targets only.

superseded_activity_id.description: The completion this session had BEFORE the current one replaced it, or 0 if none was ever replaced. `stride complete` on an already-done session overwrites `completed_activity_id` in place; the payload reports `replaced_activity` and the human line prints the command that restores it, but before this column that record lived in one line of stdout, once — so an athlete who noticed a week later had shell scrollback and nothing else. LAST value only: a second overwrite replaces it, and the cross-session case (a completion that also released another session's substitute link) is not covered here. 0 rather than absent, per the same rule as `completed_activity_id` — no activity has id 0, so the sentinel is unambiguous.

rested.description: Open rest sessions whose target_date has passed with under 1.0 load recorded on that day. Rest is the one session type whose prescription is the absence of evidence, so these are resolved in fact while still open in the lifecycle; they are excluded from still_open and from completion_pct's denominator. A rest day that DID carry load fails this test and stays in still_open — training through a rest day is a plan deviation.

data_freshness.description: Whether the facts in this payload are current, and what work is still owed before they are: measurements rather than a verdict, since what counts as too stale depends on the question being asked and ADR 0012 puts that judgement on the coach's side of the line. Present so a planning turn need not spend a second call on `doctor`.

newest_activity.description: Date of the newest activity in the database, YYYY-MM-DD, or "" when there are none. Read alongside summary.as_of, minding what that gap measures: as_of is pinned to the day `analyze` last ran, not to now, so the gap is last-activity-to-last-analyze. It equals days since the last ride only when analyze ran today; otherwise it simply stops growing. No value of it distinguishes a current install from a stale one, which is why last_sync is the primary staleness signal and this is the secondary one.

last_sync.description: When the last successful `sync` BEGAN, as a UTC ISO timestamp — the stamp is taken before the activity listing — or "" when sync has never run, when the stored value will not parse, and when it is negative. This is the payload's only full timestamp and its only UTC value; every other date here is a bare local YYYY-MM-DD. Compare it against the current date: that is the one field that detects an install where nothing has run in days.

activities_awaiting_metrics.description: How many rows `analyze` would recompute right now. Shares the predicate `analyze` selects on, so beyond rows never scored it counts rows whose FTP, threshold pace, zones, metrics_rev or underlying activity inputs have changed since they were scored — a newly arrived stream being the commonest. Never fewer than doctor's `unanalyzed`, which counts only rows with no metrics at all, and equal to it in the ordinary case. Meaningless unless activities_awaiting_metrics_known is true.

activities_awaiting_metrics_known.description: False when the count could not be computed at all — the metrics predicate needs the full zone config, and an unparseable per-sport HR-zone override makes it unreadable. The count is 0 in that case and must NOT be read as "nothing to do". `plan` deliberately degrades here rather than failing, so one bad optional config key cannot cost the whole planning bundle; `analyze` is the command that reports the underlying error.

activities_awaiting_streams.description: How many activities `sync` would still fetch streams for. Same count doctor reports as pending_streams.

strength_without_sets_ids.description: Strength-family activities from the last 30 local days with no stored sets, newest first: the ids to fetch from the Strava app log and pass to `stride strength import`. The same list doctor reports as strength_without_sets_ids.
